subject.title: [codex] Key llama.cpp sessions for local reuse

question: Should OpenClaw support TurboQuant `cache_key`/`session_id` injection, and if so should that trust boundary be local-only, explicit opt-in, or provider-plugin owned?
rationale: The code repair is straightforward only after maintainers decide whether stable session-derived identifiers may be forwarded for this provider and which owner boundary should enforce that decision.

options.title: Provider seam with trusted-local guard
options.body: Move the mutation into the provider/plugin wrapper path and only emit identifiers when the resolved endpoint is local or otherwise explicitly trusted.

options.title: Explicit opt-in compatibility knob
options.body: Add a documented provider compatibility flag for TurboQuant cache-key fields so existing custom providers do not receive new identity fields by default.

options.title: Decline core support for now
options.body: Leave the behavior to a separate provider plugin or local configuration until maintainers want a first-class OpenClaw contract for TurboQuant slot keys.

recommendation.title: Provider seam with trusted-local guard
recommendation.body: Move the mutation into the provider/plugin wrapper path and only emit identifiers when the resolved endpoint is local or otherwise explicitly trusted.

likelyOwner.reason: The current provider wrapper and payload patch seam history points to this owner path for the decision.
